text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, continuing a sharp decline from its September 15 peak of $141.22. The main driver is oil prices cooling this week as Saudi Arabia signaled it would release more crude through the Strait of Hormuz following a pipeline attack, easing supply concerns that had briefly pushed prices higher. With global oil trading at $130.80 per barrel and U.S. crude at $107.02, the market is betting that Middle East disruptions won't be as severe as initially feared—which removes one of the bullish props supporting energy stocks.

The broader context is that oil prices have been volatile but ultimately restrained by uncertainty over how long the conflict will persist. While geopolitical risk in the Middle East remains real (Saudi-Houthi clashes and reported U.S. military actions continue), market signals from both Saudi officials and the U.S. administration suggest moves toward de-escalation, which has taken pressure off the supply premium that benefits refiners and producers.
